introduction:
In Tamil Nadu, the Community Certificate (Caste Certificate / Jathi Sanrithal) is issued to certify SC, ST, MBC, BC, BCM, and DNC status.

It is a critical document for reservations in government schools, colleges, public employment, and welfare schemes. Applications can be made online through the TN e-Sevai Portal or offline at the nearest e-Sevai centre.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Service Name: Community Certificate (Jathi Sanrithal).
  • State: Tamil Nadu.
  • Official Portal: TN e-Sevai (tnesevai.tn.gov.in)
  • Application Fee: Rs. 60.
  • Pre-requisite: A valid CAN (Citizen Access Number) is mandatory to apply.
  • Approval Workflow: Village Administrative Officer (VAO) -> Revenue Inspector (RI) -> Deputy Tahsildar / Tahsildar.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Community Certificate

Format Restriction: All uploaded documents must be in PDF, JPEG, JPG, or PNG format.
Personal Proofs
  • Applicant's Photo: Passport-size photograph (Maximum size: 50 KB).
  • Address Proof: Any valid proof like an Aadhaar Card or Ration Card (Maximum size: 200 KB).
Family & Declarations
  • Community Certificate Proof: Father’s, Mother’s, or Sibling's Community Certificate (old manual certificate or digital). If no family member has a community certificate, a manual letter obtained from the VAO/RI stating your community must be uploaded (Maximum size: 200 KB).
  • Self-Declaration of Applicant: A system-generated form that must be downloaded during application, printed, signed by the applicant (or parents, if the applicant is a minor), scanned, and uploaded (Maximum size: 200 KB).
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Application via TN e-Sevai

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Portal Access: Visit the official TN e-Sevai portal (tnesevai.tn.gov.in) and click on "Citizen Login" (பயனாளர் உள்நுழைவு).
  2. Log In: Log in using your User ID and Password. If you do not have an account, click "New User Sign up here" to create one.
  3. Select Service: Navigate to "Revenue Department" and select "REV-101 Community certificate", then click "Proceed".
  4. CAN Verification: Search for your CAN number using your Aadhaar Number. Select your CAN profile, enter your Date of Birth, and generate an OTP to your registered mobile number. Enter the OTP to proceed. (Note: If you do not have a CAN number, you must click "Register CAN" and create one first).
  5. Form Details: The application form will open with details auto-filled from your CAN profile. Under "Form Details," select your Father's Community & Caste, Mother's Community & Caste, and the Requested Community & Caste (Usually, the father's community is requested).
  6. Crucial Setup Choice: The form will ask: "Whether any of the Applicant's family members possess permanent online certificate issued by competent Revenue Authority?" Select "No" for this, even if you have one. Selecting "Yes" will bypass the VAO and RI and route directly to the Tahsildar, which often leads to rejection. Selecting "No" ensures the file routes correctly through the VAO and RI for proper field verification.
  7. Document Upload: Click Submit to be redirected to the document upload page. Upload the Photo, Address Proof, and Family Community Certificate.
  8. Self-Declaration: Click "Download Self Declaration form". Print it, sign it, scan it, and upload it in the respective slot.
  9. Fee Payment: Click "Make Payment". You will be redirected to pay Rs. 60 via UPI, Net Banking, or Credit/Debit Card.
  10. Download Receipt: Once payment is successful, download the acknowledgment receipt containing the Application Number (starting with TN-...) for tracking.
Offline Visits involved: While the process is online, if you do not have any ancestral community certificates to upload, you must make an offline visit to your local VAO or RI office to obtain a manual verification letter, which you will then scan and upload.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Offline Application via e-Sevai Center / CSC

Step-by-Step Offline Process:
  1. Visit Center: Visit your nearest Government e-Sevai Maiyam (Common Service Centre - CSC), Taluk Office, or Tahsildar Office.
  2. Bring Documents: Carry the original and photocopies of all required documents (Aadhaar Card, Ration Card, Parents'/Siblings' Community Certificate, and Passport-size photos).
  3. Fill Form: Request a Community Certificate application form, fill it out with accurate details, and hand it over to the e-Sevai center operator.
  4. Operator Entry: The operator will fill out the online application on your behalf using their institutional login portal, scan your documents, and upload them.
  5. Pay Fee: Pay the application fee of Rs. 60 in cash at the counter.
  6. Receipt Collection: The operator will provide you with a printed acknowledgment receipt containing your Application Number for future tracking.
afterApplying:
After Applying — Workflow & Approval

Approval Workflow

The application will automatically be forwarded to the Village Administrative Officer (VAO). After VAO verification, it moves to the Revenue Inspector (RI), and finally to the Deputy Tahsildar / Tahsildar for final approval.

Track Status

You can track the status of your application on the e-Sevai portal using the Application Number provided on your receipt.

Notification & Download

Once the Tahsildar approves the application, you will receive an SMS alert on your registered mobile number. You can then log back into the e-Sevai portal to download and print your digitally signed Community Certificate.
